summary: Frontend-only E2E of AI Watermark Remover client-side engine. 4 REAL Gemini watermarked samples (1-1, 16-9, 9-16, 20260616.png up to 2752x1536) ALL produced detection-badge-exact ('Exact alpha map · Gemini'). Adaptive non-preset tile-scan test (mid-left blob at 80,300 on 1000x700) triggered detection-badge-adaptive as expected. Sora preset produced detection-badge-adaptive with text 'Sora (OpenAI)'. Runway multi-position produced detection-badge-adaptive with 'Runway'. Batch of 2 images processed both, ZIP downloaded as 'ai-watermark-removed.zip', per-item PNG downloaded as '1-1-clean.png'. /video route loads 'AI Video Watermark Remover' cleanly. Zero console/page errors during any processing — @pilio/gemini-watermark-remover SDK loads and runs correctly in browser. ONE HIGH-PRIORITY BUG FOUND: plain no-watermark gradient (800x600) incorrectly reported detection-badge-adaptive instead of detection-badge-none. The new 4x4 full-frame tile-scan fallback in cleanCanvas is too aggressive and produces a false positive on textured/gradient backgrounds with no watermark.

integration_issues.flow: Plain (no-watermark) image detection in Auto mode
integration_issues.issue: Pure gradient image with NO watermark shows detection-badge-adaptive instead of the expected amber detection-badge-none. The fullScanRects 4x4 tile fallback in watermarkCleaner.js triggers adaptiveCleanRegion on gradient tiles even though there is no real watermark. The guard 'maxSum/minSum >= 1.5' + coverage/coverAlpha thresholds are not restrictive enough on the full-frame fallback path. Also risks producing visible artifacts on clean images processed via Auto.

action_items: Tighten the full-frame tile-scan fallback (fullScanRects) in /app/frontend/src/lib/watermarkCleaner.js so it does NOT fire on plain/gradient images. Suggested: (a) only invoke fullScanRects when the tool.regions preset search yields zero AND some global 'watermark-likeness' pre-check passes (e.g. require a minimum count of pixels where |lum-bg|>threshold globally, or require alpha 'skewness' >= X); (b) raise coverage lower bound (currently 0.0025) or the coverAlpha threshold specifically for the fallback path; (c) require at least 2 fallback tiles to agree before declaring adaptive.
After tightening, verify the 4 real Gemini samples still hit detection-badge-exact and the adaptive_nonpreset image still hits detection-badge-adaptive.
critical_code_review_comments: watermarkCleaner.js cleanCanvas: the tile-scan fallback lacks a 'is there anything unusual in this image at all?' pre-check, so on clean gradients some tiles cross the coverage/coverAlpha thresholds by luck and mutate pixels. On real content this can create visible smudges on clean images uploaded to Auto mode.

adaptiveCleanRegion mutates the ImageData and putImageData back even when the detection is marginal — combined with the loose fallback thresholds this means false positives are also visually destructive.
processFilesSequentially awaits cleanFileToBlob (sync CPU) sequentially — fine, but the large 2752x1536 Gemini sample took several seconds; consider surfacing per-image progress; not blocking.
seed_data_creation: Created /tmp/wm_tests/{adaptive_nonpreset.png (1000x700 mid-left blob), sora_test.png (800x600 bottom-left cloud), runway_test.png (900x1200 two-position white blobs), plain_test.png (800x600 pure gradient)}. Real Gemini samples used from /app/tests/samples/.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All Playwright selectors work fine with set_input_files against the hidden input[data-testid='file-input']. The 20260616.png Gemini sample (2752x1536) completes within ~10s on this environment — 30s timeout is plenty. The one open bug is the false-positive adaptive detection on plain images (tile-scan fallback). Regression path: re-run the 4 real Gemini samples + the adaptive_nonpreset test to make sure the fix doesn't break exact/adaptive true positives. Also re-check plain gradient → detection-badge-none.
rca of the issue: cleanCanvas() in /app/frontend/src/lib/watermarkCleaner.js runs a 4x4 fullScanRects fallback whenever the Gemini exact SDK doesn't apply AND the tool's preset regions don't fire. adaptiveCleanRegion's guards (coverage>=0.0025, coverAlpha/cover>=0.18, maxSum/minSum>=1.5) were designed for known corner regions where the caller has already committed to 'watermark is likely here'. When looped over 16 arbitrary tiles of a clean gradient, at least one tile satisfies those thresholds by random luminance skew from the gradient itself, so applied becomes >0 and method='adaptive' is reported. Fix: add a global pre-gate (e.g. compute the ratio of pixels with |lum-globalBg|>K to total pixels and require it to exceed a small threshold before entering the fallback), and/or raise the fallback-specific thresholds and require agreement across neighboring tiles.
